A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable. The original appendices A–C correspond to B–D in v2, which adds an integration-cost appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results, quantitative novel-view synthesis evaluations, ablations, and appendix demonstrations of dynamic scenes and relighting.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds initialization comparisons, expanded network-configuration results and computational profiling.

M1.justification: The neural primitive architecture, analytic renderer, population control, losses and application adaptations are retained. Appendix Eq. 13 makes the existing frequency multiplier explicit, but the PDFs do not establish a changed implementation or new method component.

E1.justification: The synthetic and real reconstruction datasets, toy geometries, four dynamic volumetric effects and relighting data sources are retained. The additions vary initialization, model configuration and profiling procedures within these rendering tasks. OLAT illumination is newly specified for the existing relighting examples.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their comparator sets, and AutoInt remains the alternative integration method in Section 5.1. The added initialization and profiling comparisons reuse 3DGS. Newly cited optimization and appearance techniques are discussed as future integrations, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled 100k-random-primitive profiling protocol covering total FPS, Nsight kernel metrics and heuristic operation counts, plus a random-initialization comparison. The real-scene ablation expands from network widths to a width-by-frequency grid. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining the main benchmark protocols. Figure 4 also revises a reported teapot budget from 256 to 512 primitives, without establishing that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an initialization-sensitivity check and a multilevel integration-cost analysis. Section 5.2 expands the real-scene width ablation into joint width/frequency sensitivity and memory tradeoffs. Together these substantially extend analysis of initialization dependence, default settings and computational efficiency; the earlier AutoInt and regularization studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added random-initialization comparison does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and existing appendix table values are retained, but substantial diagnostic results are added. Initialization PSNRs are 33.36 for random-initialized neural primitives, 33.32 for random-initialized 3DGS and 33.40 for mesh-initialized neural primitives. Equal-count profiling reports 218.87 versus 546.54 FPS. The width-only PSNRs 26.96/27.21/27.29 are replaced by expanded Table 3, including 27.33/27.54/27.62 at frequency 30; these are revised ablation results, not established same-setting gains. Section 4.1 also corrects the toy-example reductions from 4× primitives/16× parameters to 16× primitives/4× parameters.

T1.justification: The dynamic-field definition in appendix Eq. 13 is corrected to include the frequency multiplier on W1(x), alongside repaired parentheses. The main closed-form integration derivation and rendering equations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: analytically integrable neural primitives, real-time splatting, and quality comparable to 3DGS with approximately 10× fewer primitives and 6× fewer parameters. The added analyses support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains how higher per-primitive computation and global-memory access are offset by using fewer primitives. It quantifies slower training at approximately 2.5 hours, or 2.5× 3DGS, and interprets the new initialization and configuration results. These refine the existing efficiency and optimization discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies checkpoint reuse for the configuration ablation, OLAT illumination for relighting, wall-clock training time, and profiling implementation details including global-memory access and operation-cost assumptions. Core training hyperparameters, hardware disclosures and the project-page address are retained.

R1.justification: The conclusion adds connections to stochastic preconditioning by Ling et al., revised densification by Rota Bulo et al., and textured Gaussians by Chao et al. The main research positioning is unchanged. Other bibliography edits largely update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate references.

P1.justification: There are targeted prose revisions, a renamed Section 5.2, clearer metric descriptions, expanded concluding discussion and an added appendix section. Author/header information and bibliography formatting are cleaned up. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds configuration and profiling Tables 3–4, corrects Figure 4's primitive-count label, clarifies several captions and redistributes existing figures and tables. Existing figure imagery is retained. Conference headers, spacing and appendix table numbering also change without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The initialization check, expanded configuration ablation and integration-cost analysis strengthen support for the practical design choices and explain the efficiency tradeoff more clearly. Quantified training costs improve transparency, and the Figure 4 and resource-ratio corrections improve accuracy. These are useful targeted gains while the principal benchmark evidence and contribution remain unchanged.
